name: e2e_pdf_methods_excerpt_c1: wash, separate, lyse, incubate
description: UNROUTED. Built by assay2chip/stages/s6_build.py from partition.json: op 2 wash -> polygon_chamber 'wash_2', ops 4 separate, 5 collect, 6 wash -> polygon_chamber 'separate_4', ops 8 separate, 9 collect, 10 wash -> polygon_chamber 'separate_8', ops 12 separate, 13 collect -> polygon_chamber 'separate_12', op 14 lyse -> trap_chamber 'lyse_14', op 16 incubate -> trap_chamber 'incubate_16'. wash, mix, separate, collect, lyse, incubate share one board; they run between 25 and 37 C; 15 ports, which the target envelope does not cap; 5% of the envelope 127.76 x 85.48 mm (target envelope), ONE fluidic layer at ONE 0.3 mm etch depth, base and lid 0.5 / 1 mm. COP (Zeonor 1060R) because hot_embossing route; 90 C max working temperature covers the 37 C hold; DNA adsorption Low: hydrophobic, little DNA binding; protein/enzyme adsorption possible. The hottest hold here is 37 C. SIZED FROM THE LOAD, never from the paper's tube volumes (assay2chip/README.md, 'Bench volumes do not transfer'): wash_2 from 2,000 cells at 1500 per uL = 1.33 uL of suspension; separate_4 from 2,000 cells at 1500 per uL = 1.33 uL of suspension (the largest load of op(s) 4, 5, 6: op 4); separate_8 from 2,000 cells at 1500 per uL = 1.33 uL of suspension (the largest load of op(s) 8, 9, 10: op 8); separate_12 from 2,000 cells at 1500 per uL = 1.33 uL of suspension (the largest load of op(s) 12, 13: op 12); lyse_14 from a stated packed bed of 28.0616 uL; incubate_16 from a stated packed bed of 28.0616 uL. ONE PART PER PLACE (chip/designs/README.md rule 1): ops 4, 5, 6 (separate, collect, wash) all act on the same cells in 'separate_4', so they share one chamber sized for the largest of their loads and held at each temperature in turn; ops 8, 9, 10 (separate, collect, wash) all act on the same cells in 'separate_8', so they share one chamber sized for the largest of their loads and held at each temperature in turn; ops 12, 13 (separate, collect) all act on the same cells in 'separate_12', so they share one chamber sized for the largest of their loads and held at each temperature in turn. PLACEMENT: parts sit in flow order in 1 row(s) (left to right), spread across the usable 121.4 x 79.1 mm so the slack between them is routing corridor. Total chain length 516.8 mm, crossing risk 0, nothing rotated; every feature keeps at least 0.4 mm to its neighbours and to the chip edge. PORTS: 4 (inlet_1, outlet_1, reagent_in, waste), each over a PORT PAD the registry sized, so the bore opens entirely onto cut area and the port-overlap rule in tools/check_chip_spec.py passes. Inlets and outlets are on opposite edges, which is what keeps the layout planar in one layer, and no two ports are closer than 5 mm. CHANNELS BETWEEN PARTS ARE DELIBERATELY EMPTY: S7 routes them from assay2chip/work/<id>/connections_e2e_pdf_methods_excerpt_c1.json. Until it has run, a chamber here is unconnected on purpose, and every rule that needs a channel - channel width against capsule diameter, channel crossings, protocol targets - can only be checked after S7. REALISED AS CHANNELS, not as parts: op(s) 3 (mix) - op(s) 3 (mix) carry a stream and nothing states a residence time, so there is no length or volume to build to; realised as the connecting channel rather than as a part; op(s) 7 (mix) - op(s) 7 (mix) carry a stream and nothing states a residence time, so there is no length or volume to build to; realised as the connecting channel rather than as a part; op(s) 11 (mix) - op(s) 11 (mix) carry a stream and nothing states a residence time, so there is no length or volume to build to; realised as the connecting channel rather than as a part; op(s) 15 (mix) - op(s) 15 (mix) carry a stream and nothing states a residence time, so there is no length or volume to build to; realised as the connecting channel rather than as a part. A conduit is sized from flow and residence time, and one that comes out smaller than a face a channel can attach to is not a small part but an unusable one, so it becomes the channel instead, lengthened to the length it needs. Parts sized by assay2chip/parts/registry.py. RISKS carried from sizing: Z TOLERANCE: the gap is 25 um and published z tolerance on these processes is +/-20 um, which is +/-80% of it, so the weir could close or leak outright. blocks.json calls this the biggest unknown in the retention scheme: coupon 21, 24 and 27 um gaps before committing. If it fails, the lever is capsule size (tunable 35-260 um), which buys a proportionally larger gap.; flow distribution across a wide weir is explicitly NOT scale-free (blocks.json target_envelope.not_scale_free); this crest is 9.67 mm wide.
